full_judgment:
Mr. Borhanuddin, J:-This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties no. 1 to 7 to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 15.09.2010 passed by the learned Additional District Judge. 2nd Court. Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal no. 28 of 2001 affirming the judgment and order dated 30.04.2001 passed in Miscellaneous Case no. 01 of 2000 by the learned Additional Senior Assistant Judge (In Charge) rejecting the case as not maintainable under order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set aside and/ or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. Being aggrieved the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 207 of 1992 in the Court of learned District Judge, Comilla. After contested hearing, the learned District Judge allowed the appeal and decreed the suit vide judgment and decree dated 4.5.1996 Against the said judgment and decree, the contesting defendants preferred revisional application being Civil Revision no. 3866 of 1998 before this division wherein the order of the learned District Judge has been affirmed. Thereafter the predecessor of these petitioners, Aheda Khatun, defendant no. 18 of the partition suit, filed Miscellaneous Case no. 1 of 2000 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure stating that she is a co-sharer in the suit schedule land but no notice/ summons of the Partition Suit and Title Appeal was served upon her. In the said miscellaneous case the contesting opposite parties no.1-7 without submitting any written statement filed an application under Order 7 Rule 11 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure contending inter-alia that the partition Suit no. 82 of 1991 being dismissed the plaintiff opposite parties as appellants preferred Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla. After hearing the contesting parties, the learned District Judge allowed The appeal by setting aside the judgment passed by the learned senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Comilla and decreed the suit which was ultimately affirmed by the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction. It has also been stated that the original decree being merged with the decree of the appellate court, the miscellaneous case under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not maintainable as barred by law. The petitioner of The Miscellaneous case filed an application under Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Both the applications were heard together and after hearing the parties the trial court rejected the application under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure holding that the judgment of the trial court and appellate court below has been merged with the judgment passed in Civil revision no. 3866 of 1998. The relevant portion is quoted herein under: 

 Against the order, the petitioners preferred Miscellaneous Appeal no. 28 of 2001 in the court of District Judge, Comilla which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Additional District Judge, Second Court, Comilla, After hearing the parties, the learned Additional District Judge, Comilla disallowed the miscellaneous appeal and thereby affirmed the order passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional court, Comilla. In the said backdrop, the present petitioners heirs of Abeda Khatun (defendant no. 18 of the partition suit) moved this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure before this division and obtained the present Rule. 

 4. Mr. Md. Ashraful Alain. the learned advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not a plaint and as such the Additional Joint District Judge committed an error of law in passing the impugned judgment and order holding that the miscellaneous case order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is barred by law under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate referred the case of Harunor Rashid Talukder Vs Md. Mahbubur Rahman Talukder and others, reported in 1 MI.R(AD) 286. 

 7. On perusal of the record it appears that the defendant no. 18 of the partition suit filed Miscellaneous Case no.1 of 2000 under order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil procedure stating that she is a Co-sharer of the suit schedule land but the plaintiff without serving any summon notice upon her filed an application in the suit praying for exemption from service of summon upon her and obtained an order beyond her knowledge, It has also been stated that she was not at all aware of the proceedings of the Partition Suit no. 186 of 1986 which was renumbered as Partition Suit no. 82 of 1991 and also the proceedings of Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992. It has been further stated that notice/summon of the Title Appeal no. 207 of 1992 was also not served upon her. 

 8. The application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being not a plaint, application under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil procedure shall not apply. Therefore, The trial court has committed an error of law in entertaining the application filed by the plaintiffs under order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The appellate court below also failed to notice this legal aspect of the case in affirming the order passed by the trial court rejecting the application under Order 9 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The findings of the trial court as well as the lower appellate court that the decree of the trial court has been merged with the appellate court is factually wrong inasmuch as the suit was decreed by the appellate court. Even if, assuming but not conceding, the contention of the opposite parties accepted that the judgment of the appellate court below has311been affirmed by the revisional court and thus the suit was finally decreed that may be applicable in the case of the contesting defendants but so far the petitioner of the miscellaneous case is concerned, she having alleged that summons of the suit was suppressed and the decree was obtained fraudulently, she is not binding by the decree passed by the appellate court below is accepted, in that case, the defendant-petitioner shall be without may remedy and the plaintiffs shall be allowed to enjoy the benefit of the decree obtained beyond her knowledge and thereby she will be deprived of her fundamental and legal right to enjoy the property as an admitted co-share. 

 9. It is settled Principle of law that a proceeding under section 151 of the Code of Civil procedure cannot be taken when there are other remedies available for securing the redress in the case of punjab Ali Pramanik and others Vs. Mohd. Mokarram Hossain reported in 29 DLR(Sc) 185 our apex Court held: 

 Therefore, I find no other alternative but to interfere with the impugned order. However, I make it very clear that the decree passed by the appellate court below as affirmed by the revisional court shall be binding upon the contesting defendants as well as upon the plaintiffs and the application filed by the petitioner of the miscellaneous case in any way shall not affect the decree so far as it relates to the contesting-defendants and the plaintiffs.
